MK:
Which muscles could be affected?

Serratus anterior, pectoralis minor, latissimus dorsi

What features of the patient’s presentation could be consistent with each of these muscles?

Serratus anterior: unable to raise arm or reach for things with it

Pectoralis minor: unable to reach with arm (protraction of scapula)

Latissimus dorsi: unable to reach (\*extension of arm possibly affected (not specified in HPI which directions of reaching are impaired), although patient’s ability to adduct arm is highly suggestive that this muscle is not affected)

Which muscles are unlikely to be affected?

Pectoralis major, teres minor, subscapularis

What features of the patient’s presentation suggest that these muscles are not likely to be involved?

Pectoralis major: patient can adduct arm and rotate it

Teres minor: patient can rotate arm

Subscapularis: patient can rotate arm

For each test performed above, identify the muscle(s) being assessed

| **Test** | **Muscle Assessed** |
| Abduction of arm from 90˚ to overhead | Serratus anterior |
| Internal (medial) rotation of arm | Pectoralis major, subscapularis, latissimus dorsi |
| External (lateral) rotation of arm | Teres minor |
| Protraction of scapula | Serratus anterior, pectoralis minor |
| Adduction of arm | Latissimus dorsi (major), pectoralis major |
| Extension of arm | Latissimus dorsi |

Based off of these results, which muscle is most likely affected?

Serratus anterior

Damage to which nerve could cause the patient’s symptoms and affect the muscle listed above?

Long thoracic nerve

Why is this nerve particularly susceptible to damage?

It runs along the surface of the serratus anterior muscle and passes through the region targeted in the surgery.
